stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives an Ativan prescription issued 20 days ago by a properly authorized Connecticut practitioner. The pharmacist verifies the prescription and prescriber. What is the key determination?

choices.text: Reject it after five days under the Schedule II narcotic rule.
The prescription falls within the 30-day out-of-state Schedule IV pathway after verification.
Use the federal six-month clock as the only deadline.
Accept it without verification because Connecticut licenses the practitioner.
Require a Massachusetts prescriber for every Schedule IV prescription.

related_facts: lorazepam (Ativan) is used for anxiety disorders and short-term relief of anxiety symptoms; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.

An authorized out-of-state practitioner may issue a Schedule III through VI prescription filled in Massachusetts within 30 days of issue; Schedule III through V prescriptions require pharmacist verification.
